clue.text: Officer knowledgeable about voucher

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer
to be 'up on' a subject is to be well informed about it

explanation.surface: An officer who knows all about vouchers, perhaps a quartermaster checking the paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a ticket or slip exchanged for goods or a discount, which is a kind of voucher.

clue.text: Collier harbours terror of psychic

indicators.note: to harbour is to hold within, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner
dread is great fear or terror

explanation.surface: A coal miner nursing a terror of someone who claims supernatural powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collier' looks like a surname or a coal ship but is a coal worker; 'harbours' fits the ship reading, but signals holding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychic claims to perceive other people's thoughts, which is exactly what a thought-reader does.

clue.text: Concerned with stout correspondent

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
porter is a dark beer, close kin to stout

explanation.surface: A writer of letters who cares about dark beer, or a portly penfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' seems to describe a person but is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper correspondent is a journalist who files news stories from a place or on a subject.

clue.text: Burn old note to make a gesture

parts.note: burn and beck are both northern words for a stream

explanation.surface: Setting fire to an old banknote as a dramatic gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' reads as setting fire, but here it is the Scottish word for a stream, matched by the northern English BECK.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon is to signal someone to approach with a wave or nod, a summoning motion of the hand.

clue.text: Dominate finest horse

parts.note: best means the finest
to horse is to mount or ride on horseback

explanation.surface: The best horse dominates the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' looks like a noun but is taken as the verb, to ride.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand astride something with legs either side is to tower over it, so it figuratively means to command or dominate.

clue.text: Caught spoiling sweet

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
harming means damaging or spoiling

explanation.surface: Someone caught ruining a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' reads as a pudding but is the adjective, delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet and charming are synonyms for a delightful, pleasing manner or appearance.

clue.text: Sacked a politician for inflammatory release

parts.note: to be fired is to be sacked from a job
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is sacked for releasing an incendiary statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflammatory release' sounds like a provocative press statement, but it is a gas that literally catches fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is the methane released in coal mines, which can ignite and explode, so it is a combustible discharge.

clue.text: A crazy, upwardly mobile architect

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving upwards means the word for crazy is read from the bottom up

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A crazy architect with social ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Adam was an 18th-century Scottish neoclassical architect.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Adam is a famous Georgian designer of buildings and interiors, so the surname fits an example of the profession.

clue.text: Look both ways

definitions.note: a quick glance or peek is one kind of look, and the word for it is a palindrome

indicators.note: the answer reads the same whichever way it is read, so the clue describes a palindrome

parts.note: a quick glance or peek is one kind of look, and the word for it is a palindrome

explanation.surface: A road-safety instruction: look both ways before crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to take a quick, furtive glance, a brief kind of looking.

clue.text: Agent without sleep is irritable

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the agent wraps around the sleep

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A secret agent deprived of sleep gets tetchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking, but here it carries its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy can mean curt and short-tempered, inclined to speak sharply, which is being irritable.

clue.text: Recommend against commander breaking an engagement

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A

indicators.note: breaking into means going inside, so these letters split the other pair

parts.note: a date is an appointment or engagement
V is short for versus, against
OC is officer commanding

explanation.surface: Advice against letting a commander interrupt a betrothal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' suggests marriage but is just an appointment, DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a course of action is to argue publicly in favour of it, which is to recommend it.

clue.text: Suggestive of the latest wrap-around dresses

indicators.note: wrap-around says one word is wrapped around another, enclosing it

parts.note: recent means newest, the latest
minis are short dresses or skirts

explanation.surface: Fashion talk: the newest wrap-around dresses recall an earlier style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrap-around dresses' reads as a garment style, but 'wrap-around' is the containment signal and 'dresses' are short skirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reminiscent of a thing brings it to mind, evoking or recalling it.

clue.text: Our stamina is restored here

indicators.note: restored means put back into working order, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A patient remarks that this is where strength returns.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a place where health is recovered.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanatorium is an institution for convalescence where invalids recover their strength.

clue.text: Soldier to sack valet

parts.note: to rifle is to ransack or plunder
a man, as in manservant, can be a valet

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to dismiss his valet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' suggests firing a servant; here it means to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifleman is an infantry soldier armed with a rifle, or a private in a rifle regiment.

clue.text: Boy embraces supporter winning gold in Canada

indicators.note: winning means gaining, so the gold is attached at the end
to embrace is to hold within, so the supporter sits inside the boy

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a bra is a supporting undergarment
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A boy hugs a fan who has won a gold medal in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' suggests a fan but is a bra. The definition names a place found in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Labrador is the mainland region of the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador.

clue.text: Nun died tragically in New Zealand

indicators.note: tragically suggests things going badly wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A news report of a nun's tragic death in New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunedin is a city on the South Island of New Zealand, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Some years with conservation group are corrupt

indicators.note: with says the second piece goes alongside the first

parts.note: a decade is a group of ten years
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: An accusation that a conservation body has been rotten for years.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes moral decline and self-indulgence, a sense close to corrupt or degenerate.

clue.text: Philosopher behaved without sin? First class!

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so behaved goes around sin

parts.note: did means acted or behaved, as in 'did well'
to err is to sin
A means first class, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: Someone behaved without sin? Excellent!
explanation.walkthrough: 'without sin' reads as innocence, but 'without' means outside: DID surrounds ERR.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Derrida was a French thinker, the founder of deconstruction, so he is an example of a philosopher.

clue.text: Supply post providing grub

parts.note: to cater is to supply food
a pillar is an upright post

explanation.surface: Supplying a mail post with food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food, fitting 'supply', but it is a larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is an insect larva, and a caterpillar is the larva of a butterfly or moth.

clue.text: One man takes a long time producing artistic works

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is short for male, a man
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: An artist takes forever over his works.
explanation.definitionFit: Images are pictures, paintings or representations produced by artists.

clue.text: Knowing some nuclear chemistry

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Knowing a bit of nuclear chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means slyly playful or mischievous, implying a knowing manner.

clue.text: Pulled up car making low vibrant sound

indicators.note: pulled in a down clue says the word is drawn backwards, upward

parts.note: RR is Rolls-Royce, a car

explanation.surface: A car pulling up and rumbling quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled up' looks like a car stopping, but 'Pulled' turns 'up' around to give PU.
explanation.definitionFit: A purr is the low, continuous vibrating sound a contented cat makes, or a smooth engine.

clue.text: Dismissed with less than player in game

parts.note: RO is the cricket abbreviation for run out, a way of being dismissed
under means less than, as in under ten
S is South, one of the four players at bridge

explanation.surface: A player sent off for having less than the rest in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Rounders is a British bat-and-ball game, rather like baseball. S as a player needs bridge, where the four seats are North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounders is a bat-and-ball team game played mainly in British schools.

clue.text: Conflict by the sea, briefly gave enthusiasm

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces stand side by side

parts.note: war is armed conflict
Med is the short form of the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A seaside war stirs up enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: To be warmed to an idea is to be made keen, so warming someone instilled enthusiasm or heart.

clue.text: Hear a gun going off in lecture

indicators.note: a gun going off is fired, and the letters likewise explode into a new order

explanation.surface: Hearing a gunshot during a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' fits the gun but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a long, forceful speech of reproof, a scolding sermon.

clue.text: More enthusiastic mourner

definitions.meaning: a professional wailer at an Irish funeral, one who laments the dead

explanation.surface: A grieving person throwing themselves into the funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the comparative of keen and an Irish term for a hired funeral wailer.
